statement: A patio is made of a rectangle that is $20$ feet long and $12$ feet wide, plus a semicircle whose diameter is one of the $12$-foot sides of the rectangle. What is the total area of the patio, in square feet?

choices.misconception: I added a full circle of radius $6$, but the patio has only half a circle.
I used $12$ as the radius of the semicircle instead of its diameter, so I got $\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot 12^2 = 72\pi$.
I used $12$ as the radius and also added a full circle instead of a semicircle, which gave $\pi \cdot 12^2 = 144\pi$.

hints: Split the patio into a rectangle and a semicircle.
The rectangle's area is length times width. The semicircle has diameter $12$, so find its radius and take half of $\pi r^2$.
The semicircle has radius $6$, so its area is $\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot 6^2$.

solutions.reliable: The rectangle has area $20 \cdot 12 = 240$ square feet. The semicircle has diameter $12$, so its radius is $6$ and its area is $\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot 6^2 = 18\pi$ square feet. The total area is $240 + 18\pi \approx 296.5$ square feet.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
